title: Identities and composition for unique logarithmic infinitesimal lifting
statement: For arbitrary log schemes and the fine strict square-zero tests of [def-sfb-log-infinitesimal-lifting-properties], the identity log map has unique global infinitesimal lifts. If $f:(X,L)\to(Y,M)$ and $g:(Y,M)\to(Z,N)$ each have unique global infinitesimal lifts, then their constructed composite $g\circ f$ [lem-sfb-log-morphism-operations] has unique global infinitesimal lifts. No Noetherian or saturation assumption is imposed on endpoints or tests.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69 and X 1.2, pp.136--139; Kato 1988 3.1--3.3. Explicit uniqueness argument by F3.

proof.text: For an identity test square the bottom map is a lift, because the top composite with the identity equals the top map. Any lift must equal the bottom map by the identity triangle equation.

For a test square of g after f, first use the unique lifting property of g with top map a followed by f, obtaining cY. Use the property of f on the square with bottom cY, obtaining cX. Associativity verifies both triangles for cX. Any other lift has intermediate composite cY by uniqueness for g, and is then equal to cX by uniqueness for f.
